scope.question: Which source-defined catalytic-group perturbations retain a measured endpoint, and which apparent comparisons cannot be transferred?
scope.evidence: Projection of accepted source annotations; not new measurements, an independent evaluation, protein admission or evidence-tier promotion.
scope.selection: All rows of the accepted RA95 2013 kinetic and stereoselectivity tables and RA95 2017 kinetic panel; all six RA61 Table4 construct rows; all five KE59 Table2 pH-profile rows and its unassessed E230-control question. The beta-barrel packet is outside this bounded relation. One source-reported RA95.5-8F methodol synthesis outcome and its two precursor comparator contexts extend product evidence with separate conversion, isolation and source-assigned composition records. A Siegel2010 Diels-Alder extension adds three parent kinetic parameters and two author-reported activity-reduction factors with unqualified assay/metric; product bounds remain separate source contexts.
scope.arithmetic: Source-rounded central values, same-source assay and background only; reported efficiencies are never replaced by kcat/KM division.
scope.identity: Exact sequence/provider availability is separate from study-declared construct association and physical assay-specimen identity.
scope.limitations: No pooled rates, generic inactivity labels, causal residue assignments, full apparatus claims, microscopic coupling energy or design-success estimates. Forward product composition retains source-author configuration and unresolved retention mapping; strict ee bounds remain structured source context, not central-value comparisons. Diels-Alder activity-reduction summaries do not identify mutant kcat or product outcomes; strict product bounds and mismatched assays remain in context.
